An almond mom is a mother who imposes unhealthy eating habits and harmful expectations about weight and body image onto her children, especially daughters. In plain terms, she is a parent who is so consumed by diet culture — the obsession with being thin, eating "perfectly," and controlling weight — that she pushes those same ideas onto her kids, often causing real harm in the process.

In the world of an almond mom, diets reign supreme, being skinny is highly valued, and if you're hungry, a couple of almonds should do it.
Where Does the Term Come From?

The story behind the name is very specific, and understanding it makes the whole concept click instantly.

In a video compilation featuring old clips from the reality TV show The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills, Yolanda Hadid is shown in 2014 talking on the phone with her then-teenage daughter, Gigi — a famous fashion model. "I'm feeling really weak. I had, like, half an almond," a shaky-sounding Gigi tells her mother. Yolanda's response? "Have a couple of almonds, and chew them really well."

Think about that for a second. Gigi was already so hungry that she had eaten only half an almond, and was feeling physically faint — and her mother's advice was to simply eat a few more almonds. Not a proper meal. Not even a real snack. Just a handful of almonds, chewed slowly. This response struck millions of people as a perfect example of a mother who has so deeply internalized unhealthy ideas about food and thinness that she genuinely couldn't see how harmful her advice was.

The "Almond Mom" expression was first coined after a compilation of Yolanda and Gigi Hadid was shared on TikTok on July 6th, 2022, where Yolanda is repeatedly seen discouraging her daughter from eating. The video resulted in a huge uproar, with many people beginning to call Yolanda Hadid and other moms with an obsession for diets "Almond Mom."

Yolanda defended her controversial comment in an interview, explaining that she was recovering from surgery and "half asleep" when Gigi called. She also acknowledged her now-infamous advice by posting a TikTok of herself snacking on almonds while doing a variety of activities, including yoga, with the caption "#worstmomever #almonds" — clearly poking fun at herself.
How Did the Term Go Viral?

The term became popular on TikTok in late 2022 and early 2023 as part of a trend in which users, often jokingly, depicted almond moms with overly strict or dangerously unhealthy eating habits. Users often used the term to describe their own parents or people they knew.

The creator @tyler.benderr on TikTok played a key role in giving the term its official definition: "An almond mom is a mom who is a little bit bought into diet culture. A little bit of an obsession with healthy eating, with her body image, with her daughter's body image. Maybe a little bit of an obsession with fitness. But it tends to veer on the side of overdoing it." Since then, #almondmom has gone viral, with billions of views on TikTok of kids sharing their examples of "almond mom" comments like: "I see you're having a sandwich, are you sure you want two slices of bread?"

The meme gave people a shorthand to describe the way so many of them felt growing up in homes where every bite of food and every snack was watched and judged. Creators made viral videos capturing the various sayings familiar to those who grew up in diet-obsessed households — directives like, "You're not hungry, you're just bored," or more subtle remarks such as, "I can't believe you're eating that. I'm still full from breakfast!"
What Does an Almond Mom Actually Do?

An almond mom is not necessarily cruel or obviously mean. An almond mom isn't necessarily someone who outright tells their kids to eat less and lose weight. Instead, this type of parent tries to help their kids be "healthy." They criticize extra cookies on a plate or comment on the growing waistline of a neighbor not to shame anyone — they've just been taught to value size as an indicator of wellness.

According to one pediatrician and childhood obesity expert, an almond mom is a person who is usually "stuck in diet culture," and likely grew up hearing phrases such as "a moment on the lips, a lifetime on the hips," and "you're not hungry, you're bored." The almond mom phenomenon is rooted in fat phobia and internalized bias. She projects her own fears onto her children and, in doing so, teaches them that she doesn't accept them unless they're at a weight that may be unattainable.

Some recognizable behaviors include constantly commenting on what, how much, or when children eat; labeling foods as "good" or "bad"; talking negatively about her own body in front of her children; watching portion sizes obsessively; and tying a child's worth or attractiveness to their weight or size.

As one clip from the same show also showed, Yolanda told Gigi on her birthday: "You can have one night of being bad, right. Then you gotta get back on your diet, though. Because, you know, in Paris and Milan they like the girls just a tad on the skinny side." This is a textbook almond mom comment — framing normal eating as "being bad" and tying a child's professional worth directly to being thin.
The Deeper Cultural Context: What Is "Diet Culture"?

To fully understand the almond mom, you need to understand the environment that creates her. Diet culture is the widespread cultural belief that thinness equals health, beauty, and moral goodness. It is what causes people to see food as something to be controlled, feared, or earned rather than simply enjoyed for nourishment and pleasure.

The almond mom parenting style is one centered around harmful eating advice deeply rooted in 20th-century diet culture. The almond mom didn't just invent these ideas herself — she absorbed them from her own upbringing, from magazines, from advertising, from a society that relentlessly told women (and girls) that their value lies in how thin they are.

Their intent is far from malicious. They were sharing attitudes that were culturally normal in the environments they grew up in. Parenting is an incredibly challenging journey, and it's unreasonable to expect perfection, especially when many mothers have never known an alternative perspective. This is an important point: an almond mom is usually not trying to hurt her children. She genuinely believes she is helping them. The tragedy is that the very ideas she was raised to think are healthy and caring are actually harmful.
Why Is This Term Important? The Real-World Harm

The reason "almond mom" became such a powerful term is that it put words to something millions of people experienced but never had a label for. And the harm it describes is very real.

Almond moms can have a very negative impact on their kids — children can develop a bad relationship with food, strong anxiety around food or fear of eating, and this can lead to disordered eating or severe eating disorders in the future. It can also have a knock-on effect on self-esteem and mental health. Research published in the Journal of Law, Medicine & Ethics concluded that observing the eating behavior of others influences children's acceptance of foods, while findings from Cambridge University suggested that mothers who were preoccupied with their own weight and eating reported higher levels of restricting daughters' food intake — which may place daughters at risk for developing problematic eating behaviors.

A "well-meaning" dieting mindset causes shame, guilt, and fear around food that can stick around for life. Worse, this can increase a child's risk of binge-eating or other disordered eating behaviors.

By making comments like "Are you sure you need seconds?" or "This is such a cheat meal," almond moms normalize the idea that food is either "bad" or "good." This labeling breeds feelings of guilt and shame around food. Research shows that children exposed to diet culture at an early age are more likely to develop body image issues, disordered eating behaviors, and even full-blown eating disorders.

Research shows that when parents model negative self-talk about their own bodies, follow restrictive diets, and comment on the bodies of others, their kids adopt similar mentalities and follow similar disordered eating patterns — even if those negative comments or food restrictions were never directly aimed at them.

Growing up in a home where dieting, disordered eating, and poor body image are normalized can have serious impacts on children's mental and physical health. Disordered eating patterns can lead to anxiety, depression, and social isolation. Additionally, children may internalize the poor body image attitudes they are exposed to and begin to view their own bodies in a negative light.
Is Being Called an "Almond Mom" Always Negative?

Almost always, yes. The term is almost always used as a negative one to criticize a person as endangering themselves and their families with poor nutrition and insufficient diets.

However, the term has evolved slightly on the internet. The term has also broadened to refer, sometimes positively, to a concern for nutrition and fitness, as in "Every time I visit, my parents make sure they have my favorite almond mom foods, always stocking up with fresh veggies, sugar-free yogurt, and organic snack bars." In this lighter usage, people sometimes jokingly call any health-conscious food habit "almond mom behavior." But this is the lighter, more humorous use of the term — the core meaning remains a serious criticism of diet-obsessed, food-controlling parenting.

The language around this concept has expanded naturally:

A male counterpart to almond mom is almond dad. Other relations, such as a brother or wife, perceived to impart unhealthy eating or body image habits can also be described using similar language. The term is frequently used to modify other nouns — not just in reference to a person, but to characterize various actions or attitudes, such as "almond mom behavior."

So if someone says a household has "almond mom energy" or calls a comment "very almond mom of you," they mean that the environment or the remark is rooted in that same restrictive, appearance-focused attitude toward food and bodies.

In one sentence: an almond mom is a parent — usually a mother — whose relationship with food and body image is so warped by diet culture that she unintentionally (and sometimes intentionally) passes those harmful attitudes on to her children. The term was born from a viral TV clip, exploded on TikTok, and gave millions of people a way to name and talk about something that had shaped their childhoods in ways they were only beginning to understand as adults. In recent years, Western culture has begun to embrace body neutrality, self-acceptance, and decreasing the stigma of mental health disorders, including eating disorders — and the rise of the "almond mom" conversation is a direct part of that shift.
